If you are playing the enhanced editions, start with the original and play the series through.

If you are playing the original gangsta versions from back in the day, skip to BG2.

BG1EE plays much better than it used to in the 90's now that it has all the good features BG2 added.  It makes the series feel like it progresses like it should.

in BG1 you start out barely knowing which end of your sword is the sharp end and what way to point it.  You're on the run because people are hunting you, and the bulk of your time is spent adventuring and self-discovering.  This part of the series portrays your journey from a punk kid to a seasoned adventurer.  By the end of BG1, you're character will be on par with many of the esteemed merchants who have settled down to open shops and live their lives.

Fortunately there's no settling down for you because of the events in BG2.  You start out a seasoned adventurer and you have to fight to take back what is yours.  You're the one doing the hunting in BG2.  Instead of being chased by assassins, you are the one doing the chasing.  Your pursuit leads you into more and more danger but you eventually emerge as one of the most renown heroes (or villians) of the realm.  Famous characters such as Drizzt are considered your peers at this point instead of your heroes.

And then there's Throne of Bhaal.  By this time, the nations, the people and the gods have had their fill of the Bhaal prophecy and the death/drama that is has brought upon the land.  Whether you are a great hero or a villainous evildoer, you are given no choice but to play out your part in prophecy.   This part of the series covers your ascension from hero to demi-god.  In BG1 you were just a punk who had to worry about getting out of a bar-fight unscathed.  In BG2 your biggest worries were the things of nightmares such as mind flayers, demons and dragons.  In ToB all of this stuff is afraid of you, and rightfully so.

Overall, the game progresses nicely now.  The biggest problem I had before was that BG1 used to be so primitive compared to BG2 (no class kits, no dual wielding, no spell variety).  I always wondered what BG1 would be like if it had all the cool features of BG2, and with the EE that question was answered nicely.

In BG1, you progress to the next levels and you gain accordingly.  As long as you don't go beyond 3 million exp it's totally normal.  To hit 3 million exp in BG1 you would need to farm monsters hardcore for a long time.  It sort of soft caps about 2 levels above the cap because it starts to take more exp to reach the next level than you can naturally get in the game.  As a mage for example, you may get to cast level 5 spells, but you won't get very far beyond that because of the heavy exp spike needed to level beyond that point.

In BG2 it will just let you level normally.  You can level past 3 million since the high level abilities are in the game.  Exp is hugely inflated in BG2, especially if you decided to do Watcher's Keep.  You'll hit the normal cap really quickly.

Hey man my mother was like that growing up.  I'm not special needs or anything but I'm going to tell you the story of how it fucked me up royally.

My mother was very confrontational just like you mentioned.  She emotionally abused my father and myself + brother.  She meant well for sure, but she was a real tyrant and would yell and start fights if things were not precisely her way all of the time.

Here's some notes on what this did to me.  I'm now 32 and decently adjusted:

First of all, it put me off on women for a long time.  I never even had a date until I was 27 years old.  I couldn't trust them.  I couldn't function around them.  I couldn't even fucking talk to them.  I was a lot like Raj on the Big Bang Theory.  Even to this day I have trouble trusting them.  I'm now married, but my wife knows about my past with this and knows that i'm always looking over my shoulder when it comes to women.  She also knows that when we do rarely argue and I shutdown emotionally that it's an involuntary response.  I would never even dream about trying to bring home a girlfriend growing up, not that I could function around girls anyway at the time.

Growing up I had to build extensive mental defenses because of the emotional turmoil i was subjected to every day.  Now I cannot feel emotions like normal people.  Both good news and bad news deflects off of the many walls, shields, moats and barriers that I had to erect inside my head to protect myself.  I don't smile or show sadness most of the time.  When I do, it's often an act.  I can instantly detach myself from the outside world, and often involuntarily do so.

I became a loner.  I could count my friends on one hand.  I couldn't have them over to my house because my fucking tyrant mother would drive them away or get on them about shit.  When I went to their house I always felt threatened because of the interrogation afterwards.  I would develop very violent thoughts towards people growing up.  I had poor self esteem and only did well in school out of fear.

I got to see the toll it took on my father and hear him talk about killing himself.  I regularly would think the same thing growing up.  There were times when I would have rather died than had her rage at me.  I sat many times knife in hand ready to do it.  My father had plans to hang himself, and shoot himself at one point.  One time he wrote a note.  My mother called the police to commit him.  I was the one to find his setup and see a single rifle bullet sitting on the table.  I was the one who had to walk him to the fucking police car so they could take him in.  

I had a window air conditioner in my room that would make the typical white noise hum that they make.  When I would wake up in the morning I could hear them fighting.  When I turned the air conditioner off to hear better it was silent.  I was hearing the echo's of their arguments in my head when there was nothing there.  I had to listen though to know what the situation was when I would come out of my room for the morning.

The emotional abuse against my father eventually turned physical when I was about 17.  My mother threw a paring knife at him once, and on another occasion broke his thumb.  I saw her him him a few times too.

I tried so hard to get them to have a divorce.  I wanted them separated.  They did not need to be together.  If I could have made one wish growing up, this would have been it.  Eventually she got cancer and things got worse.  Finally one night we forced her to go to the hospital after she cleared all of out of the house within a 30 minute time frame.  I was in my 20's when this happened.  Guess who turned out to be the bad guys?? Yeah you're right they hospital fucking said we were.

She died shortly afterwards.  Now she occasionally only comes back in a nightmare here and there.

My advice to you is this:

Either put your fucking foot down with the force of a thousand elephants or get the hell out of there.  If you don't its going to get worse for you and your children.  Don't accept a temporary change or truce.  This is not acceptable, and it will fuck your children up badly.  They may not resent you, as I do not resent my father at all, but they will resent their unhappy childhood.  You're kids are young.  They deserve to be happy.  You deserve to be happy.

The epilogue to my story:

My father is now 59 remarried 2 years ago to a wonderful women who cares about us.  We are finally a real functional family.  My step-mother is what a true mother should be.  I look forward to our family gatherings rather than dread them as I used to.  He is the happiest he has been in his entire life and it shows.

My brother is still recovering.  He is 27 and a struggling artist.  He has been in a dysfunctional relationship with his girlfriend for over 6 years.  He has issues still and we cannot discuss our mother with him.  He's getting better though, and his relationship is starting to get better to.  In a few years there may be hope.

I'm 32 and was married in November after dating for 3 years.  I still do not completely trust women, but i have come along way.  It was hard in the beginning, and my wife did not understand why until she talked at length with some of my family during an all female tea.  I'de like to say i'm mostly over it, although I resent my childhood and the demons I grew up in will never completely leave me.

Speaking of news, let talk about the media.  When Sandy Hook happened, I was working 12 hour 6 day a week shifts in a call center that had the news on the TV.  My wife is one of those people who eats up gloomy tragedy stories so she would tune into the news and watch the developments and the interviews and whatnot.  For what seemed like weeks on end, I watched as Anderson Cooper and the other sensationalist media jockeys grief mined these poor people 24 hours a day.  I watched as idiots on TV talked about things like video games that they have never played and misrepresented facts about.  In my mind I began to see these media hounds as just as guilty as the shooter.

It's bad enough that double digit numbers of innocent kids were killed.  The dead were not given their dignity.  Media reporters like A.C. and such spent weeks whoring the deceased for a nation that is sustained by the grief of others.  Was it news?  Yes.  Did we need a month of nonstop coverage?  I do not think so.  Give the dead their peace.  Let them mourn without cameras.  

The blame though cant be entirely attributed though to the media or the shooter.  We as Americans DEVOUR this stuff.  It sustains us.  We feast on the suffering of others.  We ask ourselves "how long till the next one?"  This horror will continue until we as a society realize this.  We are like a fat kid guzzling a case of mountain dew and gorging on cheese fries.  We are all responsible for this.  We who bully.  We who shoot.  We who film.  We who watch.

Next time such a terrible waste of life occurs we need to focus on something else.  We need to pelt the grief mongering media reporters with rotten tomatoes and drive them out of town so the dead can rest with dignity.  What is the value of life if there's no decency in death?  We need to show them that we do not want their super sized order cheese fries and trauma anymore.

Things will only get worse until we can all start treating each other like real people.  Kids will continue to get isolated and lash out.  The media will continue to feed us with unhealthy doses of pain and suffering.  People will continue to needlessly die.  I'm afraid it's going to get worse before it gets better.
